note: How many people improve anyway, on a placebo or with time alone, for some of the uses members report on: context next to what members report, never a direct comparison (trial responders were measured on strict scales; a member's "better" is self-reported). Researched from meta-analyses and large trials, checked against each source, and shown on the library, in the community and by Sig. scripts/sync_rules.sh copies this file to the app and Sig; the website keeps its own copy (library/data/baselines.json).

uses.label: Sleep
uses.says: In insomnia trials, about 42% of people on a placebo had clearly milder insomnia after 3 months.
uses.defined_as: Improvement of at least 6 points on the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) after 3 months on placebo. The low end is the same measure at 1 month. A second drug programme used a 7-point cut-off and found 30–41% across months 1, 3 and 6.
uses.population: Adults with insomnia disorder in phase-3 trials of two orexin-receptor-antagonist sleep drugs
uses.pooled: 2 pooled phase-3 trials, 1,824 patients (638–685 on placebo with ISI data); plus 1 trial of 949 patients
uses.caveat: No meta-analysis reports placebo responder rates for insomnia, so these figures come from pooled data in two drug programmes, and the share rises the longer people stay on placebo. In a meta-analysis of primary-insomnia drug trials, placebo groups achieved about 64% of the drug's improvement (Winkler & Rief 2015).

uses.label: Other pain
uses.says: In chronic pain trials, about 38% of people on a placebo had at least 30% less pain (28–45%, depending on the kind of pain).
uses.defined_as: At least 30% reduction in pain intensity from baseline while on placebo
uses.population: Adults with chronic peripheral neuropathic pain (headline figure). The range covers fibromyalgia (low) and chronic low back pain (high) trials.
uses.pooled: Neuropathic: 50 trials, 5,693 on placebo; fibromyalgia: 30 trials, 3,846 on placebo; low back pain: 2 trials, 217 on placebo
uses.caveat: The headline comes from a large meta-analysis that is a preprint (no journal version found); peer-reviewed figures are 28–31% for fibromyalgia and about 45% for chronic low back pain. With the stricter ≥50% cut-off, placebo shares drop to about 19% (fibromyalgia), 23% (neuropathic) and 30% (low back), and range from 7% to 43% across neuropathic pain types.

uses.label: Joint pain
uses.says: In osteoarthritis trials, about 35% of people on placebo pills had at least 30% less joint pain after 12 weeks.
uses.defined_as: At least 30% reduction in WOMAC pain after 12 weeks on placebo pills. The low end is at least 50% relief on placebo pills (25%); the high end is at least 50% relief on a placebo gel (about 5 in 10).
uses.population: Adults with osteoarthritis in oral anti-inflammatory trials; mostly knee osteoarthritis in topical gel trials
uses.pooled: Oral: 7 trials, 3,554 patients (all arms); topical: Cochrane review of 39 studies, 10,857 participants
uses.caveat: The placebo response in osteoarthritis is large and depends on how the placebo is given: placebo-gel arms responded more often than placebo-pill arms (about 5 in 10 vs 25% reaching ≥50% relief). The oral figures come from one drug programme, not a meta-analysis of every osteoarthritis placebo arm.

uses.label: Mood & motivation
uses.says: In depression trials, about 37% of people on a placebo improved by half or more.
uses.defined_as: At least 50% reduction in depression score (HAM-D or MADRS) from baseline
uses.population: Adults with major depressive disorder in double-blind antidepressant trials
uses.pooled: 252 trials, 26,324 on placebo (pooled rate); range from 75 trials
uses.caveat: The pooled placebo response has stayed at about 35–40% since 1991; low–high is the spread across 75 trials published 1981–2000 (mean 30%). Trial patients have diagnosed depression and regular clinic visits, while members' 'mood & motivation' is self-rated and broader.

uses.label: Stress & anxiety
uses.says: In anxiety trials, about 39% of people on a placebo improved by the trial’s own measure.
uses.defined_as: Responder by each trial's definition, in priority order: at least 50% drop on the Hamilton Anxiety scale (HAM-A), otherwise CGI 'much' or 'very much improved'
uses.population: Adults with generalized anxiety disorder in medication trials
uses.pooled: 23 GAD placebo arms, 3,659 on placebo; 107 studies in a broader anxiety/OCD/stress-disorder meta-analysis
uses.caveat: The headline is the unweighted mean across trials, and low–high is mean ± 1 SD (no min–max was reported). A 2023 meta-analysis across anxiety, OCD and stress disorders found a similar 37%; members' 'stress & anxiety' is broader and usually milder than diagnosed GAD.

uses.label: Gut health
uses.says: In irritable bowel trials, about 38% of people on a placebo said their symptoms improved.
uses.defined_as: Improvement or cure of global IBS symptoms or of abdominal pain, as defined by each trial
uses.population: Adults with irritable bowel syndrome in drug trials
uses.pooled: 73 trials, 8,364 on placebo (pooled rate); range from 45 trials
uses.caveat: Stricter modern endpoints give lower rates: 27% for global improvement, 34% for abdominal pain and 18% for the FDA composite endpoint (73 trials, 2021). Members' 'gut health' covers much more than IBS.

uses.label: Menopause symptoms
uses.says: In hot-flash trials, about 36% of women on a placebo had at least half as many hot flashes after 12 weeks.
uses.defined_as: At least 50% reduction in the frequency of moderate-to-severe hot flashes from baseline
uses.population: Menopausal women with frequent moderate-to-severe hot flashes in placebo-controlled drug trials
uses.pooled: 2 pooled phase-3 trials, 342 on placebo; 2 further trials, 247 on placebo
uses.caveat: The placebo share builds week by week: 27% at week 4, 33% at week 8 (a separate pair of trials) and 36% at week 12. In hormone-therapy trials lasting 3 months to 3 years, hot-flash frequency fell 58% on average with placebo (24 trials), so a looser 'better' is likely reported by more women.

uses.label: Injury healing
uses.says: Most acute injuries settle on their own: in a large trial of acute low back pain, 84% of people on a placebo had recovered within 12 weeks.
uses.defined_as: Sustained recovery (pain 0–1 out of 10 for 7 days in a row) within 12 weeks on placebo. The low end is at least 50% pain relief after about a week on a placebo gel for strains and sprains ('2 or 3 in 10').
uses.population: Adults with acute low back pain seen in primary care (used as a proxy for acute muscle strain); adults with acute strains, sprains and sports injuries in topical painkiller trials
uses.pooled: 1 trial, 553 randomised to placebo; Cochrane review of 61 studies, 8,386 participants
uses.caveat: No meta-analysis of natural recovery from acute muscle strain was found, so this leans on one large placebo-controlled back-pain trial (half recovered within 16 days); its 12-week figure comes from the full results, not the abstract. Acute soft-tissue injuries mostly settle on their own, so the baseline is high.

uses.label: Tendons & ligaments
uses.short: 32% better in 6 weeks on their own
uses.says: Tendon pain often settles slowly on its own: with wait-and-see, 32% of people with tennis elbow were better at 6 weeks, and most (89%) within a year.
uses.defined_as: Trial-defined 'success' with a wait-and-see approach at 6 weeks. The low end is complete recovery or much improvement after a placebo injection alone at 4 weeks; the high end is global improvement at 1 year without active treatment.
uses.population: Adults with lateral elbow tendinopathy (tennis elbow) in wait-and-see, placebo-injection or no-treatment arms
uses.pooled: Meta-analysis: 24 trials, 1,085 untreated participants (1-year figure); headline from 1 trial of 185 patients
uses.caveat: Recovery is slow but steady: 32% at 6 weeks, 85% by 26 weeks after a placebo injection, and 89% by 1 year across 24 trials. Almost all the data are for tennis elbow; other tendons and ligament injuries may behave differently.

uses.label: Fat loss
uses.says: In weight-loss drug trials, about 20% of people on a placebo (with diet and exercise advice) lost at least 5% of their weight.
uses.defined_as: Losing at least 5% of starting body weight while on placebo
uses.population: Adults with overweight or obesity in placebo-controlled weight-loss drug trials
uses.caveat: Low–high is the 95% CI of the pooled estimate, not the trial-to-trial spread; the share rises with trial length (median 23% at 1 year). Placebo arms in these trials usually also get diet and exercise advice, so this is 'advice plus placebo', not doing nothing.

not_shown.why: The only meta-analysis is in chronic fatigue syndrome (about 20% improved on a placebo; Cho 2005, Psychosomatic Medicine), a very different group from healthy people after more energy.
Sexual-dysfunction meta-analyses report score changes or the share of successful attempts, not the share of people who improved.
No peer-reviewed meta-analysis of placebo arms gives a share of people who improved.
The adult ADHD meta-analysis (Castells 2022, 94 trials) reports an average 23% drop in symptoms, not a share of people.
